subject: general
question: What is the working principle of an analogue vibrating reed frequency meter?
solution:
The working principle of an analogue vibrating reed frequency meter is 1) Electromagnetic resonance.

**Explanation:**

The instrument contains a set of thin steel reeds, each with a slightly different natural frequency of vibration. These reeds are mounted on a common bar that is excited by an electromagnet connected to the AC supply whose frequency is being measured.

__
 
• 
 
When the AC current flows through the electromagnet, it creates an alternating magnetic field that causes the bar (and all reeds) to vibrate.

 
 
• 
 
The reed whose natural frequency matches or is closest to the supply frequency will go into mechanical resonance and vibrate with the largest amplitude.

 
 
• 
 
The frequency is read directly by observing which reed is vibrating the most.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 
 
2) Piezoelectric effect: Used in crystal oscillators or some modern sensors, not in traditional vibrating reed meters.

 
 
• 
 
3) Thermal expansion: Used in thermometers or thermal overload relays, not for frequency measurement here.

 
 
• 
 
4) Electrostatic attraction: Used in electrostatic voltmeters or certain types of actuators, not in this type of frequency meter.
